heading: COVID-19 cases prediction using regression and novel SSM model for non-converged countries
text:
- Abstract

Anticipating the quantity of new associated or affirmed cases with novel coronavirus ailment 2019 (COVID-19) is critical in the counteraction and control of the COVID-19 flare-up. The new associated cases with COVID-19 information were gathered from 20 January 2020 to 21 July 2020. We filtered out the countries which are converging and used those for training the network. We utilized the SARIMAX, Linear regression model to anticipate new suspected COVID-19 cases for the countries which did not converge yet. We predict the curve of non-converged countries with the help of proposed Statistical SARIMAX model (SSM). We present new information investigation-based forecast results that can assist governments with planning their future activities and help clinical administrations to be more ready for what's to come. Our framework can foresee peak corona cases with an R-Squared value of 0.986 utilizing linear regression and fall of this pandemic at various levels for countries like India, US, and Brazil. We found that considering more countries for training degrades the prediction process as constraints vary from nation to nation. Thus, we expect that the outcomes referenced in this work will help individuals to better understand the possibilities of this pandemic.

Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design and Technology) | BTechEE

Artificial Intelligence (AI), Computer vision and Robotics honour program gives a broad perspective of modern technologies and applications in real life. AI, when combined with robotics, allows users to build smart robots that can work independently as per inputs from robotic sensors. Artificial Intelligence and Robotics allows theory, algorithms, and systems for making intelligent decisions in complex and uncertain environments.

The course covers most aspects of artificial intelligence and robotics including perception and interpretation of sensor data, learning about environments, learning to make decisions, automated planning and reasoning, and interaction of AI robotic systems with each other and with humans. The computer vision when added to smart robotics gives true problem-solving solutions in industrial environments. Computer vision with artificial intelligence trains computers to interpret and understand the visual world. Machines can accurately identify and locate objects then react to what they “see” using digital images from cameras, videos, and deep learning models. After completing this Honours degree students will be equipped with knowledge from all the three domains and will be industry ready in true sense.

heading: Current Social Projects
text:
Project Warli

It provides a source of livelihood to the Warli artists of Dahanu, by promoting the dying tribal art form- 'Warli'. The students market the various products with warli paintings made by these artists and constantly innovate and introduce new products as per the customer needs.

Project Finlit

Under this program, basic financial literacy is imparted to the underprivileged sections of the society. At present the students are working with 3 institutes with a total of 9 batches.

Project Kruti

This is a project to empower rural women by unleashing their artistic skills and making them self-dependent. Emphasis is given on usage of locally available cotton and Kasuti embroidery (a local art-form).

Project Utsaah

It impacts BPL rural women at Nareshwadi Learning Centre and urban HIV affected women by honing their skills in garment manufacturing aprons and surgical masks. Utsaah has also won the Walmart women empowerment grant for the year 2016.

Project Drishti

Project NAB was started in 2016 and has set up a Vermicompost plant with the objective to provide an earning opportunity to the visually challenged residents of NAB Ageing Home for the Blind at Khandala.

Ankur

The Experiential Learning Initiative ‘Ankur’ was launched in 2014-15. Ankur caters to developing a robust learning environment that amalgamates all aspects of learning and provides holistic development of a management student. This course focuses on the development of emotional competencies along with managerial skills.

Access by Train

Somaiya Campus is located very near to Vidyavihar railway station which comes on the Central Railway of Mumbai, between Kurla and Ghatkopar. If you are planning to come from the Western Railway, like Churchgate, Bombay Central, you can change from the Western Railway to the Central Railway at Dadar station, and catch a slow local train from platform no. 1 or 2.

heading: Placement Policy
text:
- All the official communication related to placement from/to the TPO will be through Official Somaiya Email i.e. tpo.engg@somaiya.edu.
- Students will receive all the official emails on their Somaiya email only.
- Students will use Somaiya email only unless specified by the company for using ‘Personal email’ while registering on any company portal (if required).
- All the recruitment updates regarding test schedule, interview rounds, selection etc. will be shared from the TPO through email and/or from student coordinators through class WhatsApp groups.

- Once the TPO receives the communication from the company having details such as Job profile, Company details, Package, Location etc; the Registration Form Link specific to that opportunity is sent to all the students.
- Students are advised to submit only the valid and true information in the shared registration form. If any discrepancies are found, the student will not be allowed to sit for any future placement activity in the college.
- It is the responsibility of the student to keep checking the Announcements/notices/updated information/shortlisted names etc. sent by the placement cell during placement activity on their Somaiya individual / batch email groups.

- Students should prepare and submit their resume by using the template provided by the college at the time of registering for placement.
- The information mentioned in the resume has to be valid & genuine.
- Students should mention all the skill set, interested area and extra/co-curricular activities in their resume and keep updating it timely.

heading: Placement Policy
text:
- All the ‘Registered students’ are required to remain available all the time during the entire recruitment process, regardless of their assigned slot for interview/test.
- All the ‘Registered students’ should be present at least 15 minutes before the scheduled time of PPT/aptitude test/interview/Group Discussion.
- Late comers for any reason will not be allowed to appear for the process and will be treated as absent for that particular drive.

- Once a student has registered for a company, it is mandatory for him/her to appear for all the selection rounds of that company, unless rejected by the company at any stage.
- Any student who withdraws deliberately in the middle of the selection process, he/she will not be allowed to apply for any future placement opportunity in the college.
- Once registered, if any student remains uninformed absent, he/she will not be allowed to apply for any future placement opportunity in the college OR placement committee will decide suitable disciplinary action against that student.

- “A good first impression can work wonders” – J.K. Rowling
- It is mandatory for all students to appear well groomed in proper formal attire/work wear during the entire recruitment process including PPT. If anyone is found coming in casual/inappropriate attire, he/she will not be allowed to attend any rounds of that particular drive.
- It is mandatory for all the students to wear a college ID card during the entire recruitment process including PPT.

heading: Placement Policy
text:
- All the registered students will be allowed only 10 placement attempts
- If the student is unsuccessful after 10 placement attempts he or she must undergo PIP (Performance Improvement Phase) for a period of minimum 2 Weeks to maximum 4 weeks. Throughout this period, the student will not be allowed to participate in any placement processes.
- During PIP, the student must evaluate his/her previous performances and identify his/her weaknesses. The students should work on his weaknesses by enrolling in online or offline training workshops suggested/organized by TPO cell.
- Upon successful completion of the PIP phase and submission of the training certificates, the student gains eligibility for five additional placement attempts. However, if the student remains unsuccessful even after exhausting these additional attempts, then it means that he/she needs further improvements. The placement committee representatives will help in understanding the learning needs for further improving the student. Those students will have to undergo training as suggested by the placement committee. In the meantime the student will be excluded from the placement process for the time being. After the completion of necessary training the student will be inducted in the placement process again.

- Placement Cell organizes training/workshops on employability skills, personality development, resume building etc.
- All the final year students (UG and PG) are required to actively participate in training programs/workshops

- All the aspiring students should be prepared with adequate learning, subject knowledge and required skills related to the Job profile/company’s work domain.
- It is advised to refer to the company website to know more about the company and job you are applying to.

heading: Placement Policy
text:
- Pre Placement Talk (PPT) is conducted by the visiting company for the aspiring students to give details about job profile, service agreement, location etc.
- It’s an opportunity for students to interact with the company representatives and clarify all their doubts & concerns related to the job opportunity.
- It is mandatory for all the ‘Registered students’ to attend the Pre-Placement Talk.

- At KJSSE, we allow our students to avail Dream job opportunities i.e. Students have a chance to get 200% placement adhering to certain conditions as set by College authorities.
- Dream Job opportunity will be considered as the final job offer and 100% joining is mandatory.
- First Job Package shared during the Job Announcement/PPT will be considered for calculating Second Job Eligibility.

text:
- ? If the 1st Job Package is 10 LPA, then a student can apply for a Dream Job if its package is >= 15 LPA.

- It is mandatory for all the students to keep checking their Somaiya mails regularly and be available for call / WhatsApp during the entire process.
- It is mandatory for all the students to be available and present during the complete recruitment process as instructed and required by the company personnel.
- Students will have to report and attend the test/interview/Group discussion as scheduled by the company personnel in-person/virtually.
- After selection is confirmed by the company and informed to TPO, it is mandatory for the selected students to submit a photocopy of the offer letter to the Training & Placement Office.
- As a protocol, During/after the process, students are not permitted to directly communicate with HR or company personnel for any query or concern but only through TPO.
- Strict Disciplinary action will be initiated against students involved in any unethical practices in any stage of placement drive.
- In case of any discrepancies/dispute in placement process or placement policies, the decision of the placement committee will be final.

During / after the placement drive, if any student is found violating the placement policy, process or guidelines given by the placement cell, the student may be liable for any one or more disciplinary action in consultation with college authorities:

- He / She may be debarred from the placement process for the entire semester/year.
- He / She may not get any recommendation for further studies.
- Recommendations given for further studies may be revoked.
- Any other disciplinary action suggested by College Authorities.

heading: Circular/COE/133/2022
text: Attention: Exam Cells/Students/Faculty/Staff

heading: Subject: Unfair Means during Evaluation/Examination
text:
Reference: Circulars, notices and trailing emails

We all as a student dream about our career and we do all necessary efforts to get  admission to
desired programme of the University. The teaching learning process is well defined and we undergo
it to understand the fundamental and conceptual knowledge in chosen field of the programme.  We
learn advance topics to inculcate skills to become employable or do research and development in
our chosen career. Our parents/ guardians support financially, morally in all respect and they also
dream about our career with expectations that we will undergo programme with all efforts needed.
They expect we complete the programme with certain level of performance index i.e. SGPA/SGPI.

During evaluation/examination process we need to study certain modules and we appear for the
examination to test ourselves how much we have developed understanding, expertise and depth of
knowledge relevant to field of chosen programme. We do study and appear for the examinations.
But sometime we do lag behind the studies due various reasons and we realised that preparations
are not up to  the desired level and we try to choose the path of unfair means during the
examinations.

heading: Subject: Unfair Means during Evaluation/Examination
text:
At our university level we talk about such unfair means during examinations right f rom the
orientation to time to time instructions. We even give such instructions in our examination Time
Table and in examination hall before the commen cement of the examination. In spite of it some
students who are not able to control their mind knowingly or unknowingly selects the path of unfair
means to ac hieve the desired performance in the examinations. But we all kn ow at our university
we do not support such unfair  means of any level during the evaluation/examinations and th e
students are caught while doing unfair means. Such cases are then forwarded with well -defined
necessary documentation to College Prevention of Unfair Means Committee (CPUMC) and then
sent to University Prevention of Unfair Means Committee (UPUMC ) for  final approval. These
cases are addressed and resolved as per the sections 20,20A and 47 of exam manual for unfair
means during the evaluation/examination process.

The students are requested not to become impatient which leads to adopt the act of unfair means but
to discuss the same with parents/ guardians/teachers freely and try to get out of it. At university
level the students are free to meet any faculty/teacher/authorities to discuss. Counsellor is one of the
members of the UPUMC committee and the students can have confidential discussion with th e
counsellor any time to get proper guidelines/advice. The contact details of counsellor can be sought
from the exam cells. Many students have followed this practice and we observed its impact on the
cases reported for unfair means.

heading: Subject: Unfair Means during Evaluation/Examination
text:
The students should note that university does not permit unfair means during
evaluation/examinations and they are also requested to avoid such practice and in case if tempted to
do so it means they need to undergo counselling. For any further clarifications/ counselling required
in this regard t he students are free to contact exam cell or COE office any time  in person or under
emergency on phone.

heading: Circular/COE/134/2022
text: Attention: Exam Cells/HOIs/Faculty/Staff

heading: Subject: Reporting Unfair Means Cases
text:
Reference: Circulars, notices and trailing emails
Following are some of the acts of the student in the examination hall which are considered as unfair
means.

The mentioned acts is not an exhaustive but noted most commonly seen.

The examination
means any type of evaluation theory, practical, oral, seminar, presentation, on screen etc.
 Carrying any electronic gadgets like mobile phone, smart watch, programmable calculator etc.
 Carrying any book, notes, paper, charts or log book or data sheet or data book marked /written
material with other than printed matter etc.
 Misbehaviour, misconduct, making arguments with the supervisor/authorities, any act which is
disturbing to fellow colleagues in the examination hall etc.
 Referring to the website link, shared files/material, downloaded files/material, software tool,
use of pen drive etc. which is prohibited by the examiner during the on screen examination
 Copying from the fellow c olleagues answer sheet during the examination or observed/
realised/noted by the examiner during the assessment
 Taking any help , exchange or loan of charts or  any instruments or any other materia l from
fellow colleagues without the permission from the supervisor
 Taking help of other student/person or referring any material inside or outside the examination
hall during the examination
 Other than any commonly observed act listed above but which comes under the unfair means
In continuation to circular no 133 dated 6 th January 2023 and as per the section 20,20A and 47
of examination manual we have certain steps to report the unfair means cases during the
examination.

They are very common steps being followed across the universities/institutions.

The steps are as below
1.

heading: Subject: Reporting Unfair Means Cases
text:
If any supervisor/faculty/staff/authority finds that any student or group of students are involved
doing unfair means in examination hall it should be immediately reported to chief conduct or/
senior supervisor
2.

The chief conductor/senior supervisor  will visit the  examination hall along with the necessary
document no.

32 and new answer sheet
3.

The document 32 contains the declaration by the student and report of the junior supervisor.

The student should note that they will be given fair opportunity to defend their case/prove their
innocence during the meeting with College Prevention of Unfair Means Committee (CPUMC)
meeting.

4.

The student will be given new answer sheet on which the time of issue  will be mentioned to
continue to write the examination means allowed to continue to appear/attempt the examination.

In no case the student is asked to walk away from the examination hall  or rather it is expected
that the student did not leave the examination hall and continue appearing for the examination
5.

If required the chief conductor/senior supervisor may inform the students’ parents/guardians
before the student leaves the campus after the examination
6.

The individual student is informed with a letter (Document no.

70) with a mention about the
schedule of the meeting with CPUMC.

All such cases during the one set of examinations will
be forwarded to CPUMC
7.

The CPUMC will verify the reported unfair means cases on the case to case basis and the
student and junior supervisor or anyone who is concerned to the case are given fair opportunity
to present their stand/views/opinion
8.

The consolidated report (Document no.

71) of the CPUMC is submitted to the HOI/Dean for
recommendations and then to University Prevention of Unfair Means Committee (UPUMC) for
further process and approval  (Document no.

73).

heading: Subject: Reporting Unfair Means Cases
text:
A letter is issued to the individual student
about the decision of UPUMC (Document no.

74)
9.

The student is intimated with a letter mentioning the final decision which i s considered as a
final one.

Refer to section 20,20A and 47 for further details/guidelines

Somaiya Vidyavihar University
(Center of Examination)

Levels of Punishments
(As per Guideline Section 20A of Exam Manual

20A The different levels of punishment may be recommended by
CPUMC/UPUMC based on the fact fi ndings / detailed investigations
of the case
i.  The student shall be given warning  letter  stating not to repeat the any
type of unfair means in future and it will be endorsed by the said student
in writing
and/or
The said examination/paper/course/subject  appeared by the student
shall be considered as null and void
ii.  The said semester/term examination  in full  appeared by the student
shall be considered as null and void
iii.  The student shall repeat the semester/term  in next academic year  and
shall have to pay the requisite fee to reappear the said semester/term
iv.  The student shall be debarred for 03 (three years)  from the college and
shall be allowed to reappear the examination of the said semester/term
in full
v.  The student shall be rusticated  from the colle ge and his/her
registration/admission for the said programme shall stand cancelled
vi.  In addition to levels - i to v – HOI/Dean may recommend additional
punishment

heading: Circular/COE/221/2024
text: Attention: Exam Cells/Students/Faculty/Staff

heading: Subject: Unfair Means during Evaluation/Examination – carrying mobile phone
text:
Reference: Circulars, notices and trailing emails

In continuation to circular no 133 and 134 it is observed that in spite of repeated warnings
given the students are carrying electronic gadgets particularly Mobile Phones during the
examinations mainly with the assumption that they will use AI tools to get answers t o the
questions asked.

We have section s 20 and 47 of exam manual which clearly mentions about the guidelines
relevant to unfair means during any type of examination.

It has been repeatedly and consistently notified at various levels that carrying mobile phone
during the any type of evaluation/examin ation is considered as act of unfair means and
such cases will be reported to prevention of unfair means committee. As per section 20(D) of
exam manual in such case the student is allowed to continue to appear for the  said
examination.

We understand that the mobile phone has become very essential device to carry particularly
for students. Parents / guardians also want students to carry it. Hence exam cell do return the
mobile phone to student and the exam cell notifies to student to call parents / guardians to
inform them about the unfair means. As per section 20 (E) the exam cells is also expected to
call parents/guardian and inform them about the unfair means immediately.

The mobile phone is retu rned with the condition that the student gives u ndertaking
(Document no. 32) mentioning that the mobile is received which was carried during the
examination and will accept the decision given w ithout considering mobile as a
proof/evidence of unfair means.
